text:
A: Hiya! Oh, lovely, it's you. I was hoping I'd get you.
B: Oh, hi. Really? Sorry, I mean, hi. I'm Abena.
A: Rebecca. I'm in Exeter. How's it going so far? Have you had a call already?
B: Yeah, I had one. It was okay, erm, he was nice. A bit quiet. I think I talked too much about a book.
A: No such thing as too much about a book. What was it?
B: The Dispossessed. Ursula Le Guin.
A: Oh, I've got that! It's in the half-finished pile by my bed, which is basically a tower at this point. Is it worth getting through?
B: Yeah, definitely. The second half is kind of the best bit. It all comes together.
A: Right, okay, I'll dig it out. What are you studying? I saw the hoodie.
B: Biomedical science, first year. I'd like to go into haematology, in an NHS lab, hopefully.
A: Oh, brilliant. Why haematology?
B: Erm, there's sickle cell in my family, my wider family, so it's kind of always been there, you know? And I just like blood. That sounds weird.
A: Not to me it doesn't! I'm a vet, I spend half my life bleeding cows. Not in a horror film way. Taking samples, for TB testing and herd health and that sort of thing.
B: Oh, that's really cool. Do you do the testing yourself, or does it go to a lab?
A: Mostly off to a lab, so people like you, basically, eventually. Please be nice to my samples. They're usually a bit muddy.
B: [laughs] I'll try.
A: Honestly, lab people are the unsung heroes. I'm out in a freezing shed at three in the morning, knackered, guessing, and the lab are the ones who actually tell me what's going on.
B: My dad's a nurse, and he says the same about the lab at Broomfield. He says nobody thanks them.
A: He's right. Is he chuffed you're doing it?
B: Erm... yeah. I think he'd have liked medicine, kind of. But he's supportive.
A: Well, I nearly did medicine, and then I realised I liked animals more than people, mostly. You can't argue with a sheep. Well, you can, but it doesn't listen.
B: [laughs] Do you have pets as well, or is that too much?
A: One lurcher, Moss. That's her back end in the corner there. She stole a whole block of cheddar off the counter last week, the entire thing, wrapper and all. Proper criminal.
B: Oh no. Was she okay?
A: She was fine, smug, if anything. Do you have any animals?
B: No, not really. I've got six houseplants, and they've all got names. That's kind of it.
A: That totally counts. What are they called?
B: Erm, the monstera's called Gloria. She's just got a new leaf, actually, so I'm quite proud of her.
A: Gloria! That's amazing. See, you're way better at keeping things alive than me, I killed a sourdough starter. That's literally just flour and water and I couldn't—
B: Sorry, go on.
A: No, no, I was just going to say, Moss probably ate it.
